title: ICE Agent Shoots Man in NYC; Mamdani Calls Trump, Demands ICE Out
excerpt: An ICE officer shot 28-year-old Oscar Belgal in his car in Marble Hill on Oct. 8 while a 5-year-old child sat inside. Mayor Mamdani spent two hours on the phone with Trump and DHS's Markwayne Mullin trying to free the wounded man — then demanded ICE leave New York City entirely.
body:
• An ICE officer shot Oscar Belgal, 28, a Dominican man, around 4 p.m. on Oct. 8 in Marble Hill, NYC, firing seven rounds into his car while a 5-year-old child believed to be his son sat inside, according to Mayor Zohran Mamdani and NYPD Commissioner Jessica Tisch. The child was unharmed; Belgal was hospitalized in stable condition and later removed from the hospital by ICE agents.
  • Mamdani called the shooting "unconscionable," said he spent roughly two hours on the phone with President Donald Trump and DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin trying — unsuccessfully — to negotiate the wounded man's release, and demanded all ICE enforcement end in New York City.
  • DHS said ICE was carrying out a "targeted enforcement operation," citing a prior grand-larceny conviction, multiple prior arrests, and alleged Trinitarios gang ties — and blamed New York's sanctuary policies. The NYPD said it had no involvement in the federal operation.
  • For immigrants in NYC: the mayor's demand is a political stance, not an enforceable order over federal agents. The New York Immigrant Coalition is tracking the case and has demanded body-camera footage be released; its statements and the mayor's office are where New Yorkers can follow what happens next.

An ICE officer shot a man sitting in his car with a 5-year-old child in New York City on Oct. 8 — and within hours, Mayor Zohran Mamdani was on the phone with President Donald Trump, demanding an end to all ICE enforcement and trying, unsuccessfully, to free the wounded man.

The shooting in Marble Hill

Around 4 p.m. ET, federal agents surrounded a gray Honda CRV in Marble Hill. NYPD cameras caught the car backing into a parking spot as a plain-clothes federal officer approached the driver's-side window with his gun drawn; the vehicle then moved out of camera range, and the shooting itself was not recorded.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=060r9GGzrI8

At least one ICE agent fired seven rounds, Tisch said, striking the driver — Oscar Belgal, 28, of the Dominican Republic, per the NYPD — in the neck below his left ear. A 5-year-old child, believed by police to be Belgal's son, was in the car and was unharmed.

Responding NYPD officers found him handcuffed on the ground and gave aid, and rushed him to NewYork-Presbyterian Allen Hospital, where he arrived stable. The department stressed it had no involvement in the federal operation. DHS confirmed an officer fired during a "targeted enforcement operation" and said aid was immediately rendered, but did not say what led the officer to fire.

"Terrorize our communities": Mamdani's condemnation

Mamdani responded within hours. In an X post sent shortly after 11 p.m., he wrote that agents had surrounded the man and the 5-year-old before firing, called the shooting "unconscionable," and said he had called Trump to demand an end to all ICE enforcement in the city.

https://x.com/anadoluagency/status/2108467516674605177

"I will not stand by while ICE agents terrorize our communities. Get ICE out of our neighborhoods. Get ICE out of our hospitals. Get ICE off our streets. Get ICE away from our children."

— Zohran Mamdani, Mayor of New York City

At a late-night news conference near the scene — with anti-ICE protesters chanting behind him — Mamdani said: "There is no explanation for federal officers firing this many rounds into a car that has a 5-year-old in the car." He accused ICE of operating "with impunity," sowing "chaos and terror" across the country, and called the agency "rotten to its core" and one that "must be abolished."

Two hours with Trump — and a failed push for release

"For the past two hours, I've been on the phone with President Trump and Secretary Mullin negotiating the release of the man ICE agents shot," the mayor said. "Those negotiations were unsuccessful." Moments before the press conference, ICE had removed Belgal from the hospital: "ICE put the man in an unmarked vehicle and whisked him away."

Mamdani said he also demanded ICE leave the scene and halt enforcement in the city. Governor Kathy Hochul said she separately spoke with both and demanded any body-camera footage be released.

DHS defended the operation and attacked the city's policies, saying Belgal had "a prior criminal conviction for grand larceny, and multiple prior arrests for assault, robbery, possession of drugs, and weapons possession" plus alleged Trinitarios gang ties, and had been arrested by the NYPD on Dec. 7, 2023, then released days later under what it called "reckless Democrat sanctuary policies."

A neighborhood already on edge

Marble Hill has become a flashpoint. On Oct. 5, eight elected officials wrote to a Target on West 225th Street citing "increasing sightings" of ICE using its parking lot as a staging area; the company told USA Today it has "no cooperative agreements with ICE or any other immigration enforcement agency."

Thursday night, crowds gathered and clashed with law enforcement near the scene. The New York Immigrant Coalition called for an investigation and the release of body-camera footage, its president saying the shooting showed "ICE's violent tactics are a clear danger to all New Yorkers."

The shooting is the latest in a string of federal-agent shootings — at least 21 people had been shot during Trump's second term before Oct. 8, per an ABC News count, including two U.S. citizens killed in Minneapolis in January. It follows a month of open friction after Mullin criticized Hochul and Mamdani for not cooperating with federal immigration authorities.

Diaspora angle

The shooting lands hard in a borough with a large, growing South Asian community. Mamdani himself is of South Asian descent, and his framing of ICE as a threat to "our communities" speaks directly to immigrant families — including Indian, Pakistani, and Bangladeshi New Yorkers — wary of stepped-up federal enforcement in the neighborhoods and stores they use daily.

What's next

Several questions are unresolved: what led the officer to fire, whether body-camera footage exists, and Belgal's custody status after ICE removed him from the hospital. Whether the Trump-Mamdani working relationship survives the mayor's demand will be the first political test.
